newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Middle East leaders take stock in Switzerland.
newsitem.headline: Middle East leaders take stock in Switzerland.

text.p: Middle East leaders came to the Swiss ski resort of Davos on Friday for a weekend taking stock of progress in Middle East peace negotiations and planning out the path ahead.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived on Friday morning and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak about five hours later, both by helicopter. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will join them on Saturday, a Palestinian official said.

The occasion is the annual meeting of the World Economic Forum, where businessmen and politicians come together informally to discuss the state of the world. This year's theme is globalisation and information technology.

The Middle Easterners will make their prime appearance at the forum on Sunday and Mubarak will take the chance to vaunt the recent success of Egypt's economic policies, which have suddenly started to attract large amounts of foreign capital.

A bilateral meeting between Mubarak and Netanyahu on the sidelines, the time for which has not yet been set, will be their first since July last year and will symbolically mark the end of a bad period in relations.
Mubarak earlier accused Netanyahu of reneging on old agreements and refused to meet him again until Israel agreed with the Palestinians on the West Bank town of Hebron.

The Hebron agreement, signed earlier this month, did help ease the tension, though Egypt and Israel proved to be over-optimistic in their predictions that it would lead to progress in Israeli-Syrian negotiations.
Palestinian negotiator Nabil Shaath, arriving in Davos on Friday, said he did not think the talks in Switzerland would tackle the substance of the next round of peace talks.
"It's only a half-hour meeting (between Arafat and Netanyahu), though it is the first since they signed the agreement. I hope it will open up new roads," he said.

"The main issues will be to speed up the peace process and to reduce the closure (of the Palestinian territories). We'd also like to see the eight negotiating committees resuming as quickly as possible," he added.

Pressed on reports that Israel alone will decide how far its army withdraws in subsequent rounds of redeployment, Shaath said cooperation was the key. "We are partners in this peace process and partners should really agree and complement each other and coordinate," he added.

Netanyahu broke the ice in Davos by meeting Swiss President Arnold Koller and tackling Jewish complaints that Swiss banks have not told the whole truth about the fate of assets which belonged to victims of the Nazi Holocaust.
